headline: 随机延迟一秒，机器人交接不再认生
title_en: Hidden Start-Delay Randomization Makes Self-Play Handover Robust
tagline_en: A one-line random start delay on the learned partner lifts handover success with unseen partners from 31% to 80% in simulation.
summary_md:
**What it is:** A paper (CoRL 2026 HumanRLI Workshop) by Mohammad Khoshnazar, Mike Degany, Deyuan Qu, Qing Yang and Matyas Szanto. They train a Unitree G1 humanoid and a learned "giver" to hand over a parcel using alternating PPO self-play in physics simulation. The problem: the giver always offers the parcel immediately, so the receiver only learns one fixed rendezvous. When a partner it has never met starts a second later, success drops from 95% to 6%. Their fix, hidden start-delay randomization (HSD), adds a random delay to the learned partner's start — a one-line rule the receiver never observes. After 300 more updates, success with unseen scripted partners rises from 31% to 80%, with high-force contacts cut three- to five-fold.

**Why it matters:** Self-play is a cheap way to learn interaction without human demonstrations, but policies can quietly overfit to their training partner. HSD is a small, interpretable change that targets that exact failure, and the paper's paired interventions make the cause-and-effect clear.

**Can you try it without a robot?** Yes, in simulation only. The authors released code at github.com/mkhoshnam/Selfplay-PPO-handover. Training PPO self-play for a G1 will be slow on a 16GB Apple Silicon Mac, so a cloud GPU is the realistic option; reading the reward and randomization code is a good first step. Note: the paper reports simulation results only, with no real-robot experiments.

pick.title: When Will You Hand It Over? A Hidden Start Delay Makes Self-Play Handover Robust to Unfamiliar Partners
pick.one_liner: 让学出来的机器人伙伴随机延迟出手，人形机器人就能和陌生伙伴顺利交接物品
pick.one_liner_en: Randomly delaying the training partner's handoff makes a humanoid hand over objects reliably to unfamiliar partners.
pick.how_to_try: 用仓库里的 Isaac/IsaacLab 或 MuJoCo 版 PPO 自博弈来训练一个虚拟 G1 接手物品；Mac 上跑仿真会比较慢，建议用云 GPU 跑；做不到时可以先读代码理解奖励设计。
pick.how_to_try_en: Train the PPO self-play G1 handover in the repo's Isaac/MuJoCo sim; Mac is slow, use cloud GPU or just read the reward code first.
pick.reason: 用一行随机延迟规则修复自博弈策略对伙伴过拟合的问题，思路简单、对比实验做得扎实，很适合新人学习自博弈与泛化。
red_flags: arXiv 编号 2611 与 2026-11 日期可疑，疑似占位或虚构条目
仅仿真验证，没有真机实验
属于会议 workshop 论文，规模有限

top.title: NJU-R-L-Group-Embodied-Lab/SuperMimic-Repro-Sim2Real
top.one_liner: 用可求导的世界模型替代物理仿真器，教人形机器人学会跳人的舞蹈

top.how_to_try: 训练需 NVIDIA 显卡，Mac 只能读代码和看视频；可先跑 CPU 测试、看渲染 mp4。
top.how_to_try_en: Training needs an NVIDIA GPU; on Mac read the code, run the CPU tests, and watch the rendered mp4 demos.
top.reason: 开源完整、有真机跳舞视频、可学世界模型与 sim2real，但训练要 NVIDIA 显卡，且为非官方复现，复现数字与论文有差距。
red_flags: 非官方复现，严格按论文设置时分数明显低于论文
真机部署有摔机风险，Mac 无法复现核心训练

top.title: nvidia/SOMA-X
top.one_liner: 把多种人体参数化模型统一到一套姿势和骨架接口上
top.one_liner_en: Unifies several parametric human body models under one pose and skeleton interface
top.how_to_try: Mac 上装 Python 和 PyTorch 跑 demo，换个身份参数看同一段动作驱动不同体型；Mac 上无法只用 GPU 快速推理，只能降级用 CPU 慢慢跑
top.how_to_try_en: Install PyTorch on Mac, run the repo demo and drive the same motion with different identity coefficients; CPU-only means slow but workable.
top.reason: SOMA-X 是扎实的图形学人体模型统一工作，开放且 Mac 可跑，但对具身智能新进展展示价值有限，惊喜感弱。
red_flags: 本质属于计算机图形学的人体建模工具，不是具身智能进展
超过 7000 网格/秒的吞吐只在 NVIDIA A100 上成立，与无显卡定位冲突

top.title: Gamer: A Generalist Vision-Language-Action Foundation Model for Long-Horizon Real-Time Game Agent
top.one_liner: 一个用键鼠轨迹训练、能玩3D游戏的通用视觉-语言-动作模型
top.one_liner_en: A generalist vision-language-action model trained on keyboard-mouse data that plays long 3D games.
